We need to find the minimal number of character flips to transform a binary string s (even length n) into a string that can be partitioned into substrings each of even length and containing only 0s or only 1s. Each substring must be even length; the entire string must be partitioned accordingly.

This is reminiscent of the problem "Minimum Changes to Make Alternating Binary String" but with the twist that each block must be of even length. Equivalent to requiring that after changes, any run (maximal consecutive identical characters) must have even length; but careful: we can partition into substrings, not necessarily maximal; we can choose any partition with each piece even and uniform. Does this impose any extra constraint beyond "the string can be segmented into runs of even length"? Since any partition can be refined: if we have a uniform substring of length L (even), we can split it into two even substrings if L is divisible by 2? Not necessarily: if L is even, we could split into two substrings each of even length only if L >= 4 and divisible by 2? Actually splitting an even-length uniform string into two substrings yields lengths a and L-a; we need both even. So we need a to be even and L-a to be even -> L must be even (given) and a even. So we can split at any even position. Thus any uniform even-length block can be further partitioned into even-length uniform blocks. So the condition reduces to: the string after changes must be such that each maximal run of identical characters has even length (since if any run had odd length, you cannot partition that run into even-length uniform substrings: sum of even numbers is even, can't sum to odd). Conversely, if every maximal run has even length, you can partition each run into pieces of length 2 (or any even size) to satisfy.

Thus the problem is: given binary string s of even length, find minimal flips to make every run length even.
